action: Verify CI fails on a deliberately failing test in a disposable branch/check fixture and that the deploy dependency cannot bypass it.
Persist opt-in, repair enum/status defects, queue localized terminal mail, and keep raw errors behind the authenticated operation log.
Use staging fixtures to exercise success, partial failure, terminal failure after retries, no opt-in, and dry-run paths; inspect captured messages before any controlled delivery.
Verify the notification worker consumes the actual configured queue; exercise transport outage and recovery without changing a successfully completed operation to failed.
Confirm AR fallback, AR RTL/EN LTR rendering, counts, branding, and an authenticated details link that denies another user's access.
Check retried operation/notification delivery for duplicate terminal messages; add a persisted deduplication guard only if the exercised delivery path can repeat.
Document mail/worker setup, observable delivery failures, and the difference between “queued” and “delivered.”
Clear the existing formatter baseline with the repository's Pint rules.
Make the style job a required deployment dependency.
Verify the final shared revision still passes vendor/bin/pint --test.
Keep formatting-only changes distinguishable in review and document the local command; a local hook is optional.
Re-run deptrac and resolve remaining playlist violations through existing Shared contracts; do not widen forbidden dependencies or hide new violations in a baseline.

Introduce PHPStan/Larastan at a compatible, reviewed level toward level 5+, and dependency auditing with explicit high/critical finding handling. Track legacy static-analysis debt without accepting new violations; account for existing verified patches rather than blanket ignores.

Upgrade the existing probe: separate liveness from readiness, require expected status/body, set connection/request timeouts, bounded retries, and confirm the intended release is being served. Keep dependency details private. Preserve /up or adapt it deliberately; adding a second unneeded health system is not the objective.

Retain at least the previous known-good release through a proposed 24-hour observation window with disk limits; verify first-deploy behavior, failure before/after the symlink switch, relative/absolute symlink handling, and worker restart behavior.

Rehearse failed deployment and recovery in staging with compatible schema changes. Target restoration within five minutes; document that code rollback does not undo migrations or external side effects.

Pin the server host key from a trusted source and enable verification for SSH/SCP. Check provisioned PHP version against the application requirement; the script's fallback is 8.4 while CI selects 8.5.
Add concise failure notifications containing release/check IDs and no secrets; track total CI runtime toward the original <10-minute target.
Store a release checklist covering artifact identity, gates, migrations, readiness, worker state, observation, recovery, and retention.

Create a data register: profile, tokens/sessions, favorites/playlists, interactions/progress, search history, AI inquiry/usage, uploads, notifications, logs, backups, and external processors. Record purpose, location, ownership key, retention, export, and deletion behavior.

Extend existing deletion tests against that register. Verify foreign-key cascades, non-FK records, other sessions, delayed jobs that reference deleted users, avatar failures after DB commit, and recoverable cleanup without recreating the account.

Build a versioned export containing the user's included data and a manifest explaining exclusions/retention. Use a queued job for large exports, private storage, expiration, and an authenticated download bound to the requesting user.

Add export/deletion progress and understandable errors to the existing settings page; require appropriate recent authentication for sensitive actions and prevent one account retrieving another's export.

Rewrite policy/security copy from the register: cookies, engagement measurements, third-party media/AI, retention, and deletion limitations. Publish no unverified certification, compliance guarantee, or blanket data-practice claim.

Translate the controls into the currently supported locales and explain local/offline data separately. Add cookie/preferences controls where actual optional features require them; inventory actual behavior before choosing a consent design.
Test export expiration, retry, revoked access, deletion during export, cleanup recovery, and backup-retention documentation. Give each retained category an explicit owner and reason.
Inventory CRUD acceptance against real forms and routes. Record what already works, permissions, filters, hierarchy navigation, and import state; keep usable pages.

Design additive locale support consistent with repository translation conventions. Specify source Arabic, translated fields, locale uniqueness, source attribution, fallback, and readiness. Backfill AR/EN without losing current identifiers or requiring new translations to publish existing approved content.

Add ordered narrator assignment using current People lookup contracts; preserve repeated narrator positions where the source contains them. Distinguish free-text attribution, structured chain, and grade source.

Extend collection/book/chapter/record forms for the five current locales with validation and visible missing-translation status. Replace large unbounded selectors with searched/paginated choices only where catalog size requires it.

Complete bulk publish/unpublish/regrade using existing operation handlers, preview, authorization, progress, failure reporting, and optional R05 notifications. Preserve raw/source grading alongside normalized labels.
Expose import state and per-batch progress in the admin workflow; prevent incomplete imported collections becoming public through bulk or individual actions.
Verify hierarchy integrity, duplicate references, invalid grade input, missing narrator targets, authorization, locale fallback, bulk partial failure, and rerun behavior.
Have an editor exercise one collection → book → chapter → record → publish → correction journey in AR and one LTR locale; document the workflow.
Trace collection → book → chapter → record paths and empty states against published, hidden, importing, and partially translated fixtures.

Present source Arabic, selected translation or explicitly labeled fallback, grade with its source, narrator attribution, and hierarchy breadcrumbs without mixing editions or implying an absent translation exists.
Connect structured narrator profiles when available through the Shared lookup contract; preserve a readable text chain without waiting for R10.
Audit per-record canonical URLs, unique titles/descriptions, locale alternates, sharing references, and pagination SEO. Fix stale ID-based links against the actual reference route contract.

Verify search queries for each current supported content language, collection filtering, Arabic normalization, empty results, and counts. Record relevance gaps for R09 rather than creating a second search engine.
Exercise Arabic RTL and LTR layouts at 360 px, tablet, and desktop widths; check long Arabic text, keyboard navigation, focus, loading/error states, and no horizontal clipping.
Add regressions for public visibility across detail/list/search/counts and for missing-locale behavior; have an editor validate sample rendered records and references.
Restore missing Hadith/companion providers and real activity avatars.
Define every card's count and scope: all admin records, published records, translations/editions, distinct surahs, companions versus all people. Display labels that match those definitions.
Implement missing series/quick metrics through the provider contract, including seven-day content activity and content growth; distinguish creation from publication and choose a consistent timezone.
Replace synthetic constants and misleading fallback zeros on active paths. Return a distinguishable “unavailable” state for failed providers and report the exception with module context.
Apply bounded caching and mutation invalidation to expensive aggregates; verify refresh after import/publication. Inspect the unused sample controller's references before any cleanup.
Test empty data, mixed publication state, provider failure, timezone boundaries, cache refresh, and no N+1 activity avatars. Measure the agreed dashboard load scenario.

Produce a source manifest: edition ID, language, author/reciter, attribution/rights, format/version/checksum, expected coverage, current coverage, and gaps. Map the proposed Sahih International, Pickthall, Yusuf Ali, Turkish/French/Urdu and remaining translations explicitly.
Trace existing commands and supported inputs; document one supported operator path for each content type. Keep generic JSON unsupported unless a concrete user workflow requires a defined schema.
Test a bounded import twice and after interruption. Verify stable unique keys, preserved curated edits, resumability, invalid-row quarantine, and no duplicate editions/verses/audio.
Add preflight validation for source identity, verse references, expected counts, missing/duplicate rows, and text integrity. Separate staging/imported state from public readiness.

Connect import jobs/progress to existing admin operations: current phase, processed/total where knowable, errors, retry/resume, terminal result, and optional notification. Never show 100% before validation/publication finishes.
Fill the approved inventory toward 10 translations, 3 tafsirs, and 5 reciters; report per-edition completeness and audio URL/timing availability rather than counting empty catalog rows.
Validate representative text with an editor, check full canonical coverage programmatically, and reconcile browser/search/cache behavior after publication.
Document recovery: isolate a failed edition/version, resume safe batches, restore prior content mapping, and retain an import manifest/audit report.
Inventory enabled versioned routes by method, path, authorization, token abilities, throttling, locale, pagination, and response resource. Separate browser/admin endpoints and disabled future routes.
Choose a supported OpenAPI 3.x authoring/validation approach after a small route/resource pilot; document why annotations, generated extraction, or a maintained spec best match the code.

Describe request constraints, success and error envelopes, 401/403/404/422/429 responses, filters, sorting, IDs, and canonical references. Preserve the difference between public liveness and authenticated content APIs.
Create sanitized examples for each current supported locale, including fallback/missing translation, pagination, and visibility exclusions. Never embed live tokens or users' content.
Add spec validation and representative request/response contract checks in CI; compare route inventory against documented operations to catch drift.

Publish a versioned spec and documentation UI. Configure “Try it” for an explicit environment with user-supplied credentials; label destructive operations and keep server-side authorization authoritative.
Add version/change notes and an owner/update rule for every API behavior change.

Define output fixtures for Arabic only, translation only, both, reference inclusion, plain text, formatted text, and academic citation including translator/edition attribution.
Extract/extend one pure formatting path using canonical verse data and selected edition; add a preview and persist reasonable format preferences.
Add bounded contiguous multi-verse selection with explicit range labels; validate start/end, preserve order, and handle unavailable translations without silently substituting another edition.
Wire clipboard and available native/platform sharing to that formatter. Encode share URLs safely, avoid duplicating reference text, and clearly identify when a platform only receives a link.
Handle clipboard denial/unavailable APIs with a selectable-text fallback. Confirm copy success only after the API succeeds; distinguish opening a share destination from actually posting content.
Verify Arabic marks, whitespace, ranges, long text, locale references, quotation formatting, keyboard focus, mobile share behavior, and the absence of Tajweed/display HTML in copied plain text.
Inventory current behavior and define one state model for source, reciter, surah/ayah, playlist, repeat mode, range, speed, position, and auto-next preference.

Produce a coverage matrix by reciter/recording: per-verse audio, full-surah audio, timing source/version, missing segments, and bismillah/intro offsets. Expose supported synchronization only for the applicable recording.
Complete next/previous, repeat one/range, continuous playback from any verse, and the required 0.5/0.75/1/1.25/1.5 speeds without conflicting with playlist auto-next.

Reconcile verse highlighting and scrolling on seeking, reciter changes, browser navigation, restored sessions, and playback completion. Stop automatic scrolling when the user intentionally reads elsewhere and provide a return-to-current action.
Version and validate saved state; clear unavailable tracks and prevent one account's private playlist state leaking into another session. Handle corrupt browser storage and blocked autoplay.
Exercise delayed/missing audio, failed timing lookup, end-of-range boundaries, rapid repeated taps, background/foreground changes, and mobile gesture controls.
Review synchronization samples against the recording and agree a timing tolerance from the source quality. Add deterministic boundary/transition tests plus manual device audio checks.
inventory persisted topic morph aliases, orphan links, and the current Hadith route/model contract. Define a migration/report for legacy aliases instead of dropping unknown rows silently.

restore Hadith type registration at the composition layer; implement current record mapping and counts through a domain-safe lookup/provider, with correct canonical URLs, grade fields, and localized text.

test display, counts, edit/save, hidden/importing collections, deleted records, missing locale, and orphan references. Confirm no forbidden cross-domain imports; remove obsolete dead mapping only after the replacement is covered.

Define a related-content reference contract: type, canonical ID/URL, localized title/excerpt, visibility, relationship explanation/source, and reviewer/version. Add Seerah and People support through their providers.
Extend admin topic assignment with searched selectors, ordering, duplicate handling, preview, and review/audit information; preserve existing verse/article behavior.
Add bounded, paginated/lazy related-content surfaces to Quran, Hadith, Seerah, and companion pages. Keep public visibility identical in lists, counts, caching, and detail links.
Curate at least 50 distinct reviewed relationships with source rationale and coverage across the requested modules; a reciprocal display of one edge is not two curated relationships.
Test publication/unpublication invalidation, missing providers, empty results, bounded query counts, and locale-aware fallback; document the editorial workflow.

Build a proposed 100-query judged set covering exact references, Arabic with/without diacritics, morphology, names, transliteration, current languages, cross-language intent, misspellings, and no-result cases. Review expected results and relevance grades.
Record current top-result accuracy, recall@10/nDCG@10 where labels support them, no-result rate, endpoint p95, and query cost on a named corpus and load mix. Separate each language/module.
Fix demonstrated query/visibility/count defects and tune current indexes/ranking first. Add curated synonyms and autocomplete with explicit query length/rate limits and privacy-aware analytics.

Run a bounded Elasticsearch comparison only if important cases remain unmet. Test Arabic normalization/stemming, proper names, exact canonical references, language fields, and curated synonym behavior against the same judged set.

Record the engine decision using measured relevance/latency, resource cost, freshness, availability, and maintenance effort. If the current engine meets the agreed requirements, close the evaluation with an explicit proposal to revise the original Elasticsearch-specific scope.

Implement index schemas/versioning, initial backfill, after-commit update/delete processing, idempotent reindex, lag monitoring, and an alias switch. Recheck public visibility before returning stale indexed results, especially after unpublication.

Explain cross-language matching behavior explicitly: aligned translations/approved aliases first; evaluate additional translation/semantic retrieval separately. An Arabic analyzer is not a cross-language translator.
Validate the agreed <200 ms p95 target, relevance thresholds set after baseline, freshness, engine outage, zero results, and stale publication state; retain the current search path for rollback.
Inventory chain sources, order conventions, missing narrators, alternative chains, repeated positions, and availability/provenance of birth/death/place/reliability data.
Define a response contract preserving source order and per-position identity; link multiple positions to the same person without merging the chain nodes.
Build a server-rendered ordered text view first, with names, known metadata, source attribution, and clear unknown/uncertain values.
Add a progressive graph with keyboard-accessible node actions, pan/zoom/reset, responsive layout, focus management, and reduced motion; link to existing person profiles.
Distinguish narrator assessments from a Hadith's grade and distinguish multiple source assessments. Describe recorded completeness/missing segments without an invented completeness percentage.
Test empty/long/branched/repeated-person chains, missing profiles, uncertain dates, private/unpublished records, RTL/LTR labels, touch controls, and JavaScript-disabled fallback.
Have an editor verify sample chain order and displayed reliability statements before enabling the graph for the full supported catalog.
Map current retrieval, provider fallbacks, quota reservation, token/cost recording, history retention, and admin reporting. Identify actual gaps before adding new stores.

Add Hadith retrieval through a Shared contract that returns canonical references, text/translation, source grade, collection visibility, and provenance; bound retrieval size and use current approved content.
Add user-owned conversation/follow-up context with maximum turns/tokens, explicit reset, and retention/export/delete integration. Treat retrieved documents as content rather than instructions.

Validate citation IDs against retrieved records; prevent invented links or a claim of source support when the cited passage does not substantiate the answer. Explain insufficient evidence and disputed/unknown grading.
Build a reviewer-scored evaluation set covering Quran/Hadith questions, follow-ups, ambiguous prompts, missing evidence, misleading source text, citation mismatches, and unsupported languages.

Extend existing cost/usage reporting for both retrieval types and conversations. Define per-user quota, token caps, provider timeout/retry, monthly budget alerts, and accounting behavior for failed/retried requests.
Evaluate the proposed 30 monthly inquiries and 500 input characters against measured quality/cost/abuse scenarios; make the change configurable and enable it only after the gate is met.
Verify cross-user isolation, concurrent quota requests, provider outage/fallback, unpublication, export/deletion, and safe error feedback; pilot with reviewed users before wider exposure.
Inventory event-to-location relationships and date representations. Record precise/approximate/unknown coordinates, date ranges/calendar conventions, source evidence, and missing geography.
Curate the required 50 events with verified locations or explicitly approximate regions; omit unsupported exact pins rather than guessing.
Define a lightweight public map API with bounds, filters, clustering inputs, localized labels, provenance, and publication-safe related references.
Select a map renderer/tile source using attribution, permitted usage, accessibility, payload, privacy, and operating cost. Document the choice before enabling third-party requests.
Add chronological navigation that handles Hijri/date ranges and uncertain order correctly; label journeys as documented routes or schematic connections according to evidence.
Build marker details, related links, filters, clustering, zoom/touch controls, and an equivalent sortable event list; support RTL/LTR labels and reduced motion.

Test overlapping/absent coordinates, large marker sets, narrow screens, tile outage, missing translations, hidden events, and range filtering. Obtain editorial approval of displayed geography and dates.

define representative route journeys and data volumes: Quran reader/translations, Hadith browse/search, topics, dashboard, and relevant authenticated operations. Record hardware, versions, database sizes/indexes, locale mix, and cache configuration.

run proposed 18- and 60-virtual-user scenarios with a documented arrival/think-time model, warm-up, sustained measurement window, cold/warm cache variants, and concurrency-safe test data. Record p50/p95/p99, throughput, error rate, query count/time, memory, and saturation.
Enable bounded/sampled slow-query diagnostics for >100 ms queries with sensitive bindings removed; capture representative query plans. Set per-route query budgets from the baseline.
Rank hotspots by user impact and total cost. Fix N+1 loads, excessive result sets, repeated lookups, and demonstrated missing indexes before adding a new distributed service.

Validate candidate composite/covering indexes against actual filter/sort/join patterns and write cost. Inspect locale/publication/reference/slug indexes without adding redundant indexes indiscriminately.
Test warm-cache mutation invalidation, concurrent requests, imports, and queue contention; avoid achieving fast stale/incorrect responses.
Repeat the same scenarios after each meaningful optimization batch and compare results, including error/throughput regression. Retain scripts, fixtures, query plans, and baseline artifacts.
Decide whether remaining limitations justify R16, R21, R17, or R09 engine work; document the expected improvement and how it will be verified.
Identify specific expensive cacheable queries/routes from R20; compare the present cache with Redis in staging, including connection overhead, hit/miss behavior, and memory.

Document topology, credentials/network access, capacity, eviction, persistence, health monitoring, ownership, and cost. Separate disposable cache from durable queues/session state; different logical databases alone do not isolate instance-wide eviction or failure.
Specify cache keys by content version, locale, relevant query inputs, visibility, and authorization where applicable. Limit whole-response caching to appropriate public responses.
Prove mutation/import/unpublication invalidation and stampede control. Preserve versioned invalidation; do not use global flush as normal application behavior.
Introduce the cache change behind environment/configuration control and verify a bounded database-recompute path or controlled unavailable response during Redis failure. Prevent recompute overload.

Evaluate session and rate-limit migration separately: coordinated multi-instance state, logout behavior, limiter guarantees, and outage policy. Do not silently switch these to per-host files when Redis fails.
Measure hit ratio, eviction, memory, command latency, database load, and the R20 p95 scenarios; exercise node outage and recovery.
Cut over selected public caches first, observe, and expand only after evidence. Record an explicit accepted/deferred decision for each proposed session/limiter change.
Inventory jobs and queues: duration, priority, idempotency key, retry/backoff, timeout, side effects, and latency expectations. Separate short user-facing work from long imports and tracking.
Measure enqueue-to-start time, queue depth/oldest age, attempts, terminal failures, and worker utilization on the current driver; fix absent consumers and configuration mismatches first.

Design worker allocation that reserves capacity for short important work without starving other queues. Verify every named queue has a consumer; long imports do not belong in a blanket high-priority stream.
Align effective job/worker timeouts, retry_after, and supervisor shutdown grace. Use workload-specific connections where incompatible timeout requirements justify them.

Exercise idempotent side effects, retry/backoff, after-commit dispatch, worker death, duplicate delivery, poison jobs, and authorized failed-job replay. Do not promise exactly-once execution from a driver switch.
Provision durable Redis capacity separately from evictable cache, migrate dispatch in a controlled window, and drain/consume old database queues until empty. Record which driver owns in-flight jobs.
Verify short-priority-job p95 pickup <1 second under the agreed workload, worker restart/deploy recovery, no stranded jobs, and monitored error/age thresholds.
Document rollback: stop new dispatch to the failing destination, keep appropriate workers draining both stores, reconcile in-flight IDs, and preserve failed-job evidence.

Inventory assets and call sites: Spatie originals/conversions, custom encrypted originals/variants, public images, private/user uploads, and Quran audio/source ownership. Record URLs, byte size, checksum, access rules, and whether caching/redistribution is permitted.

Prove an adapter for the custom encrypted path using bounded streaming or controlled temporary files, correct encryption metadata, cleanup, and authenticated delivery. Keep decrypt keys server-side and distinguish object encryption from public CDN response caching.

Design public versus private origins, access checks/signed delivery where needed, object keys/versioning, cache headers, content types, and origin restrictions. Avoid caching authenticated plaintext as public content.
Implement a manifest-based copy/verify migration: original ID, source/destination, checksum, bytes, variant state, retry status, and URL mapping. Pilot both media systems before bulk transfer.

Validate thumbnails/WebP, conversion retries, audio range requests/seeking, correct 206 responses, content length, CORS where required, and old-URL compatibility. Confirm encrypted media remains readable and private assets remain protected.

Switch new uploads and then verified existing batches using per-asset disk/location metadata; support dual reads during migration. Retain source files until verification and the retention window pass.
Measure origin load, transfer latency, cache hit ratio, errors, storage/request/egress cost, and invalidation behavior. Configure actionable budget alerts.
Exercise partial transfer, corrupt object, unavailable origin/CDN, expired access, deletion propagation, and rollback to local reads; produce an operations runbook.
Document existing event/streak behavior and define what counts as reading/listening/completion by module. A page view is not automatically verified reading.
Add user-selected goals with accessible controls, timezone/day boundaries, progress periods, opt-out, and sensible defaults; keep existing metrics authoritative.
Define grace/freeze/missed-day rules and test daylight-saving/timezone changes, late events, duplicate events, multiple devices, and deliberate goal edits.
Track per-module progress using stable references and idempotent events; explain partially completed or unavailable content. Integrate export/deletion/retention.
Add a small, explicit badge rule set with deterministic evaluation and private-by-default visibility; prevent users replaying events to inflate progress.
Introduce leaderboard participation only by separate opt-in, with a chosen display identity, withdrawal, and abuse controls. Avoid implying scores measure religious merit.
Add optional daily reminders through R23 preferences, including quiet hours/timezone and deduplication; goals remain usable without notification permission.
Test user ownership, deletion, opt-out, backfill accuracy, and understandable empty/error states; evaluate actual usefulness before adding more reward mechanics.
Define the supported browser/device matrix and install/offline scope. Create a valid manifest, icons, names, colors, start URL, and scope; verify deployment under HTTPS.
Add one versioned service worker for approved static assets and an offline navigation fallback. Explicitly bypass admin, auth, profile/export, token-bearing API traffic, and personalized HTML.
Coordinate worker activation/cache versioning with deployment. Avoid forcing an update that discards in-progress reading; provide an update/reload action when needed.
Provide bounded recently viewed public Quran content for offline use under a clear cache contract, then share data/version APIs with R24 rather than creating competing stores.
Test installation/launch on the supported Android/iOS/desktop paths, direct deep links, online→offline navigation, cold start, old-worker/new-assets combinations, and storage clearing.
Add push permission only through an explicit user action in R23; never request it on initial page load. Document browser support and the non-push fallback.
Provide a recovery/release path for a faulty worker: serve an updated worker that unregisters/cleans affected caches when appropriate, verify recovery on reload, and retain normal web navigation.

Define a bounded event catalog: newly published subscribed content, approved admin operation results, and chosen reminders. Specify recipient eligibility, deduplication key, event version, and visibility checks.
Store durable per-user notifications/subscriptions with read state, pagination, expiration, and indexes. Dispatch after content/operation commit and recheck eligibility before delivery.
Add an accessible bell/inbox, unread count, mark-one/all-read, empty/error states, and safe links. Reconcile counts across tabs/devices using server state.
Add preferences per category/channel, unsubscribe, quiet hours/timezone, and browser-push opt-in; distinguish existing bulk-operation opt-in from a new global subscription.
Begin with bounded polling when adequate. Evaluate live delivery need/latency before choosing WebSockets; keep authenticated channels and polling fallback if adopted.
Add PWA push as an optional transport with explicit permission, subscription lifecycle, revoked/expired endpoint cleanup, and minimal lock-screen payloads.
Test duplicate events/retries, deleted/unpublished targets, cross-user channel access, opt-out during fan-out, unread races, transport outage, and deleted accounts.
Observe dispatch lag, retries/failures, duplicate rate, and queue load; integrate retention/export/deletion and document operating ownership.

Define downloadable packages: selected surahs/juz and editions, bookmarked Hadith, and supported favorite content from other modules. Specify IDs, schema version, checksum, publication/version metadata, estimated bytes, and excluded asset types.
Create an IndexedDB schema and package manifest with migrations, atomic completion markers, progress/cancel/resume, and retry. Keep incomplete or corrupt packages out of “available offline.”
Add a download manager showing actual/estimated size, available-space estimate, selected editions, download state, offline badge, and manual remove/clear controls.
Define storage policy for pinned versus recent content, quota failure, and browser eviction. Request persistence only with a clear user benefit; do not promise browser storage is permanent.
Scope personal favorites/progress by account and clear/invalidate them on logout/delete/account switch. Separate public downloaded text from account activity; explain what stays locally.

Define mutation sync with operation IDs, server versions, tombstones, and deterministic favorite add/remove conflict rules. Queue offline actions and reconcile when the app reconnects; background sync is an enhancement, not the only path.
Refresh content versions and revoked publication on reconnect. Explain that a previously downloaded public copy cannot be instantly recalled while a device remains offline.
Test airplane-mode cold launch, partial downloads, quota exhaustion, complete browser eviction, schema upgrade, clock skew, two-device conflicting changes, expired login, deletion, and recovery.
Inventory runtime locale configuration, translation keys, translated content tables, hard-coded strings, email/API messages, dates/numbers, fonts, and search behavior.
Set a launch coverage matrix per language and module: complete navigation/account/security/admin UI, named initial content editions, source reviewers, and explicit fallback policy.

Source and review Indonesian, Malay, and Bengali UI/content translations; keep source/translator attribution and approved edition IDs. Use placeholders only in internal development, never as claimed coverage.
Implement locale configuration, switcher persistence, routes/alternate metadata, fonts, pluralization/formatting, and LTR UI with Arabic excerpts maintaining their own direction.
Extend imports/search/indexes and test mixed Arabic/local-language content, missing translations, long labels, and language-specific normalization where relevant.
Verify all admin forms, account/export/delete controls, emails, reader flows, offline manifests, and validation messages through the coverage matrix.
Have native-language reviewers sign off each locale; launch languages independently when their matrix is satisfied and keep incomplete ones out of the public switcher.
Establish maintenance/review ownership and connect to R26 if volunteer translation is chosen.

Define eligible contribution types, source/licensing terms, attribution choices, locales, review roles, and publication authority. Begin with bounded corrections/translations rather than every content field.
Store immutable submissions with target/version, original/proposed text, source rationale, locale, contributor, timestamps, and state history; keep canonical text unchanged while pending.
Add authenticated submission UX with preview, validation, duplicate/spam controls, rate limits, and an explicit status page. Avoid exposing private reviewer notes.
Build the reviewer queue with assignment, diffs, approve/edit/reject/request-changes, conflict detection when source content changed, and logged rationale.
Publish approved revisions atomically through existing domain services; apply cache/search/offline version invalidation and retain a reversible revision record.
Add attribution consistent with contributor choices and R28 deletion/retention policy; distinguish deleting an account from retaining an approved public editorial revision.
Implement a modest translation memory from approved segments with provenance and human selection; prevent automatic reuse from misrepresenting context or overwriting reviewed text.

Add optional contributor recognition/leaderboard with consent and abuse review. Define any later trusted-contributor privilege separately, with scope, audit, revocation, and evidence of reliable moderation.
Test authorization, concurrent reviewers, stale target versions, malicious markup, duplicate submissions, rollback, withdrawn attribution, deleted accounts, and notification preferences.
Pilot with a limited contributor/editor group, measure review backlog/turnaround/reversal rates, and expand only with enough editorial capacity.
